title: Universal Website Lifecycle

stages.objective: Understand the business, users, website objectives, and constraints.
stages.exit_condition: Sufficient validated context exists to propose a plan.

stages.objective: Assess existing digital assets and systems when applicable.
stages.exit_condition: Existing assets and critical dependencies are documented or explicitly unresolved.

stages.objective: Define scope, priorities, success measures, and execution approach.
stages.exit_condition: The proposed scope and required decisions are approved.

stages.objective: Define information, functional, and technical structures.
stages.exit_condition: Critical dependencies and architecture risks are resolved or gated.

stages.objective: Prepare content, interaction design, and visual design.
stages.exit_condition: Relevant content and design approvals are obtained.

stages.objective: Build or configure the approved website.
Verify requirements, functionality, accessibility, performance, security, and integrations.
stages.exit_condition: Release-blocking defects are resolved and required approvals exist.
Deployment is verified and ownership is transferred.

stages.objective: Monitor, maintain, measure, and improve the website.
stages.exit_condition: Ongoing; individual improvement cycles have defined completion criteria.

rules: Lifecycle stages may overlap or iterate.
Not every project requires every stage at the same depth.
Existing-site projects require an appropriate baseline audit.
High-risk actions require applicable approval gates.
Deployment is not equivalent to project completion.
Post-launch monitoring and maintenance ownership must be defined.
